judgment.rationale: Both Skills are Grade R (rank 0) statements in EMERGENT READING under the Sub-strand Phonological/Phonemic Awareness: the first ('Identifies rhyming words in well known rhymes and songs and in sequences of rhyming words') is scoped to Term 4, the second ('Recognises initial spoken sounds especially at the beginning of own name') to Term 2. judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R Skills about left-to-right, top-to-bottom directionality, but at different points and in different skill areas. The second SFI (Grade R, Term 1, Emergent Reading / Emergent reading skills) is embodied, pre-literate practice: 'Participates in directionality activities such as moving the body left to right and top to bottom'. This is substantive extension from whole-body/gross-motor orientation to a graphic, page-bound writing convention requiring finer control and an internalised spatial rule, so proficiency in the Term 1 body-movement activity supports success in the Term 2 emergent writing skill. Within Grade R the permitted developmental direction runs from the earlier Term 1 item (second) to the later Term 2 item (first), hence second_to_first rather than the reverse. judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 1 (rank 1), Term 3, Skill Area 'Reading and Phonics', but in different sub-strands: the first is a Phonics bullet ('Recognises common consonant digraphs (sh, ch and th) at the beginning of a word'), the second is a Group Guided Reading bullet ('Uses phonics, context clues, and structural analysis and sight words when reading'). This is not mere repeated wording: the first is a specific decoding element (digraph recognition at word onset), while the second applies phonic knowledge together with context clues, structural analysis and sight words to connected text during guided reading. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade 2 (rank 2) Skills in the WRITING skill area. The first sits in Term 2 under the 'Handwriting' sub-strand ('Copies and writes different formats of writing (short invitations such as birthday; messages; lists etc)'), with LCs for both copying and writing short functional texts. The second sits in the later Term 4 under 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' ('Writes at least two paragraphs (ten sentences) on personal experiences or events such as a family celebration'). Within the same grade this is an earlier-Term to later-Term direction, which is permitted, and the change is substantive rather than mere repeated wording: short, modelled/copied formats of a few lines develop into sustained, independent multi-paragraph composition on personal experience. Fluent, legible production of short written formats plausibly supports success in producing ten connected sentences, so buildsTowards first_to_second is supported; the different sub-strand focus (handwriting-based copying vs independent composition) keeps confidence moderate. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each), so the judgment rests on the supplied bullet text, identity scopes and LCs only.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 1 Skills (rank 1) resting on the same letter-sound/phonic knowledge: the first is Term 3, Reading and Phonics, sub-strand 'Daily Phonic Activities' ('Revises word families using short vowel sounds learnt'), the second is Term 1, Writing, sub-strand 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' ('Writes words using letter sounds learnt'). Their shared LC tokens ('learnt', 'sounds', 'using') and the shared 'phonics' LC tag reflect genuine cross-skill-area coherence: encoding words with learnt sounds and revising short-vowel word families reinforce one another. However, the evidence does not support a developmental dependency: within Grade 1 a buildsTowards could only run Term 1 -> Term 3 (second_to_first), yet writing words with learnt letter sounds is an application of phonic knowledge rather than a basis for a Term 3 revision of previously learnt short-vowel word families; the Term 3 statement is explicitly revision of prior learning, not an extension of the Term 1 writing skill. Complementary reinforcement across Reading/Phonics and Writing is best captured symmetrically. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all ancestors carry merge/audit context, which limits finer-grained judgment.
